To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a Brazil nut protein that is exceptionally rich in methonine has been sequenced and the sequence information has revealed that this protein is synthesized as part of a larger precursor polypeptide.

the amino acid sequence of a Brazil nut protein has been elucidated and this protein is a member of a family of sulfur-rich proteins that are conserved in their amino acid sequences and in their arrangement of cysteines.

we have cloned and sequenced a cDNA encoding an exceptionally methionine-rich protein found in Brazil nuts, and we have shown that the protein sequence data is consistent with the hypothesis that the protein is synthesized as precursor polypeptide and that the two subunits are generated by proteolytic processing of this precursor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a novel protein from Brazil nut seeds which is exceptionally rich in methonine.
the identification of a novel sulfur-rich protein that is exceptionally rich in methonine and that is found in Brazil nut seed.
elucidating the structure and function of the Brazil nut seed storage protein, a protein that is exceptionally high in sulfur amino acids.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the methionine-rich Brazil nut protein is an exceptionally rich source of methionine.
the Brazil nut protein is a sulfur-rich protein with a high methionine content.

the sulfur-rich proteins found in Brazil nut, castor bean, and rapeseed are homologous in their amino acid sequences and that the sulfur-rich seed proteins from these three plants are encoded by genes derived from a common progenitor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the sulfur-rich proteins from Brazil nut and castor bean are homologous to each other and to the sulfur-rich protein of rapeseed, and that the sulfur-rich seed protein from Brazil nut has evolved a unique mechanism for accumulating high levels of methionine.
the Brazil nut protein is the first sulfur-rich protein to be sequenced and that it is a homologue of two previously sequenced water-soluble seed storage proteins.

we have identified a new class of seed proteins which are exceptionally rich in sulfur amino acids and which may be used as a dietary supplement to provide a high concentration of methionine to humans.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Brazil nut protein is a sulfur-rich protein, not a methionine-rich protein, and the methionine content of the protein has been overestimated in the past.
the Brazil nut protein has evolved to become a methionine-rich protein, whereas the homologs in castor bean and rape seed have retained their original sulfur-rich character.
the amino acid composition of the Brazil nut sulfur rich protein has been determined.
